rationale: Tests ability to apply the diagnostic principle that painless visible haematuria demands urgent upper-tract investigation
Reinforces the principle that a single normal cystoscopy does not close the case in painless visible haematuria
Distinguishes the surgical principle that an obstructed infected kidney requires urgent drainage before antibiotics alone can work
Tests key rule that a boy with hypospadias must never be circumcised because the prepuce is needed for urethroplasty
Reinforces that a young man with obstructive voiding should not be assumed to have BPH and treated with alpha-blockers
Tests first-line imaging choice for suspected ureteric colic — NCCT is gold standard
Tests understanding that RCC presents as a triad and that incidental detection is increasingly common
Tests management of superficial transitional cell carcinoma of the bladder — TURBT plus intravesical BCG for high-risk non-muscle-invasive disease
Tests immediate management of acute urinary retention — catheterisation is the emergency priority
Clarifies that PSA is not cancer-specific and a normal PSA does not exclude prostate cancer
